name: PC817 Optocoupler
description:
The PC817 Optocoupler is a general-purpose optocoupler with an infrared LED and a phototransistor in a 4-pin DIP package. It passes a signal across an isolation barrier, protecting low-voltage logic from high voltages and noise, and it is the standard feedback part in most switch-mode power supplies.

PC817 Optocoupler – Key Features

  • Type: phototransistor output optocoupler
  • Package: DIP-4, through-hole
  • Isolation voltage: 5000V RMS
  • Collector-emitter voltage: up to 35V (80V in some versions)
  • Current transfer ratio: 50–600% depending on grade

Applications

Makers, students and technicians use it in many kinds of projects, for example:

  • Feedback loop in SMPS and chargers
  • Isolating Arduino inputs and outputs
  • PLC and industrial I/O
  • Level shifting between voltage domains
  • Power-supply repair

Usage Tips

Pin 1 (dot) is the LED anode and pin 2 the cathode; pins 3 and 4 are the emitter and collector. Use a series resistor for the LED, for example about 330–470 ohm from 5V.
